# HAlertDialog

> Confirmation dialog with a safe initial cancel action and responsive bottom-sheet layout.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.7.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HAlertDialog` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-alert-dialog>`.
- Constructor: `HearthAlertDialogElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Feedback.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HAlertDialog.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Cancel is the initial focus target. confirm requests the destructive operation; application code owns busy/error and closure on success. Escape/close emits cancel and update:open(false). Mobile uses the shared bottom-sheet breakpoint.
- mobileBreakpoint sets the mobile viewport threshold in CSS pixels. Per-component props override the inherited --h-mobile-breakpoint value from HTheme; the fallback is 640px. Set 0 to keep desktop presentation. The breakpoint updates live across Vue and custom-element shadow roots.

## Public API

open, title, description, confirmLabel, cancelLabel, danger, busy, mobileBreakpoint

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    open?: boolean;
    title: string;
    description?: string;
    confirmLabel?: string;
    cancelLabel?: string;
    danger?: boolean;
    busy?: boolean;
    mobileBreakpoint?: number;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ confirmLabel: "Confirm", cancelLabel: "Cancel" }
```

### Events

update:open(boolean), confirm(), cancel()

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:open": [
        open: boolean
    ];
    confirm: [
    ];
    cancel: [
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

default

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

dialog, header, body, footer

Use `hearth-alert-dialog::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { HAlertDialog } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
const open=ref(false);function remove() { /* Confirm through your API, then close on success. */ open.value=false; }
</script>

<template>
  <HAlertDialog :open="open" title="Remove this session?" description="This action cannot be undone." danger @cancel="open=false" @confirm="remove" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-alert-dialog');
Object.assign(element, {
  "title": "Remove this session?",
  "description": "This action cannot be undone.",
  "danger": true
});

element.addEventListener('confirm', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```

- [HButton](../button/llms.txt): Native button or link behavior, clear focus, icon-only labels, and restrained press feedback.
